ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A frictionless track contains a loop of radius $R=0.5 \mathrm{~m}$. Situated on top of the track lies a small ball of mass $m=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ at a height $h$. It is then dropped and collides with another ball of mass $M=5 \mathrm{~kg}$.

<image_1>

The coefficient of restitution for this collision is given as $e=\frac{1}{2}$. Now consider a different alternative. Now let the circular loop have a uniform coefficient of friction $\mu=0.6$, while the rest of the path is still frictionless. Assume that the balls can once again collide with a restitution coefficient of $e=\frac{1}{2}$. Considering the balls to be point masses, find the minimum value of $h$ such that the ball of mass $M$ would be able to move all the way around the loop. Both balls can be considered as point masses.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a smooth downward-sliding track, and a ball of mass m is located at a position with height h from the bottom horizontal track; on the bottom horizontal track there is a ball of mass M; on the right side is a vertical circular loop, with radius R marked, and the bottom of the circular loop is tangent to the horizontal track. Therefore the motion process can be read as: m is released from rest from height h, after sliding down it collides on the horizontal section with the stationary M, and afterward M enters the circular loop and goes around. Reasoning: The downward-sliding section and the horizontal section before collision have no friction, so the speed of m before collision is u = sqrt(2gh). The collision is a one-dimensional collision, M is initially stationary, and conservation of momentum and coefficient of restitution e=1/2 give the speed of M after collision as V = ((1+e)m/(m+M))u = ((3/2)*2/7)u = 3u/7. There is uniform friction μ=0.6 inside the circular loop. Let θ=0 be at the bottom of the circular loop, θ=π be at the top, and set y=v^2. When the ball moves on the inside of the circular loop, the normal force is N = M(y/R + g cosθ). The energy differential equation along the arc length R dθ is (1/2)M dy = -MgR sinθ dθ - μN R dθ, therefore y' + 2μy = -2gR(sinθ + μ cosθ). Use the integrating factor exp(2μθ) to integrate from 0 to π. Let a=2μ, then y(π)e^{aπ} - y(0) = -2gR ∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ, so y(0)=e^{aπ}y(π)+2gR I, where I=∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ. The minimum condition is just maintaining contact at the top, that is y(π)=gR. The integration result is I = ((1-2μ^2)(e^{2μπ}+1))/(4μ^2+1). Substituting μ=0.6: e^{2μπ}=e^{1.2π}≈43.37597, I≈0.28(43.37597+1)/2.44≈5.09282. Therefore V^2=y(0)=gR(e^{1.2π}+2I)≈gR(43.37597+10.18564)=gR(53.56161). Also V=3u/7, so u=7V/3, h=u^2/(2g)=49V^2/(18g)=49R(53.56161)/18. Substituting R=0.5 m, h≈72.902 m.

A frictionless track contains a loop of radius $R=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$. A small ball of mass $m=2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed at a height $h$ and then released. It collides with another ball of mass $M=5\,\mathrm{kg}$. The coefficient of restitution for the collision is $e=\frac{1}{2}$.

Now consider the alternative case in which the circular loop has a uniform coefficient of friction $\mu=0.6$, while the rest of the path remains frictionless. method.method_draft: Use a closed-form angle-domain energy calculation for the frictional loop. First read the diagram as: ball m starts from rest at height h above the bottom horizontal level, descends a frictionless ramp, collides with stationary ball M on the flat track, and then M enters the vertical circular loop of radius R. From the text use m=2 kg, M=5 kg, e=1/2, R=0.5 m, and μ=0.6 on the loop only. The incoming speed of m is u=sqrt(2gh). For the 1D collision with M initially at rest, use momentum plus restitution to get the speed of M after impact: V=((1+e)m/(m+M))u=3u/7. For M in the loop, set θ=0 at the bottom and θ=π at the top, and let y=v^2. The normal force inside the loop is N=M(y/R+g cosθ). The differential work-energy equation over R dθ is (1/2)M dy = -MgR sinθ dθ - μN R dθ, giving y' + 2μy = -2gR(sinθ + μ cosθ). Solve this linear ODE with integrating factor exp(2μθ) from 0 to π. At the minimum, the ball just maintains contact at the top, so y(π)=gR. This determines the required bottom-loop speed V. Finally convert back to h using u=(7/3)V and h=u^2/(2g). Substitution gives h approximately 72.902 m.

推理：下滑段和碰撞前水平段无摩擦，所以 m 碰撞前速度为 u = sqrt(2gh)。碰撞为一维碰撞，M 初始静止，动量守恒与恢复系数 e=1/2 给出 M 碰后速度 V = ((1+e)m/(m+M))u = ((3/2)*2/7)u = 3u/7。

圆环内有均匀摩擦 μ=0.6。令 θ=0 在圆环底部，θ=π 在顶部，设 y=v^2。小球在圆环内侧运动时法向力为 N = M(y/R + g cosθ)。沿弧长 R dθ 的能量微分方程为 (1/2)M dy = -MgR sinθ dθ - μN R dθ，因此 y' + 2μy = -2gR(sinθ + μ cosθ)。

用积分因子 exp(2μθ) 从 0 积分到 π。令 a=2μ，则 y(π)e^{aπ} - y(0) = -2gR ∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ，所以 y(0)=e^{aπ}y(π)+2gR I，其中 I=∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ。最小条件是在顶部刚好保持接触，即 y(π)=gR。

积分结果为 I = ((1-2μ^2)(e^{2μπ}+1))/(4μ^2+1)。代入 μ=0.6：e^{2μπ}=e^{1.2π}≈43.37597，I≈0.28(43.37597+1)/2.44≈5.09282。因此 V^2=y(0)=gR(e^{1.2π}+2I)≈gR(43.37597+10.18564)=gR(53.56161)。

又 V=3u/7，所以 u=7V/3，h=u^2/(2g)=49V^2/(18g)=49R(53.56161)/18。代入 R=0.5 m，h≈72.902 m。

method.method_draft: Use a numerical shooting or threshold simulation rather than evaluating the loop integral analytically. From the diagram, model m descending from the shown height h, hitting M on the flat part, and M then entering the circular loop. For a trial h, compute m's pre-collision speed u=sqrt(2gh), then use the collision equations with M initially at rest to get M's loop-entry speed V=((1+e)m/(m+M))u=3u/7. Numerically integrate M's motion around the frictional loop using θ as the state variable: dθ/dt=v/R and dv/dt=-g sinθ - μ(v^2/R+g cosθ), with normal force N=M(v^2/R+g cosθ). Adjust h by bisection or root finding until the trajectory reaches the top θ=π with the limiting contact condition N=0, equivalently v^2=gR. This root gives the minimum h; using the given constants yields about 72.902 m.

推理：按指定的数值射击法建模。m 下滑到碰撞前的速度为 u = sqrt(2gh)。碰撞中 M 初始静止，恢复系数 e = 1/2，因此 M 碰后进入圆环的速度为 V = ((1+e)m/(m+M))u = ((3/2)*2/7)u = 3u/7，所以 V^2 = 18gh/49。

圆环内有均匀摩擦 μ = 0.6。令 θ 从圆环底部开始计，M 在圆环内满足 dθ/dt = v/R，dv/dt = -g sinθ - μ(v^2/R + g cosθ)，其中接触法向力 N = M(v^2/R + g cosθ)。对给定 h，用 V = (3/7)sqrt(2gh) 作为 θ = 0 的初速度，数值积分到 θ = π。最小 h 对应到达顶部时刚好保持接触，即 N = 0，也就是 v(π)^2 = gR。

用 R = 0.5 m、μ = 0.6、m = 2 kg、M = 5 kg、e = 1/2 进行二分射击：若 v(π)^2 - gR < 0，则 h 太小；若 v(π)^2 - gR > 0，则 h 太大。收敛时得到所需圆环入口速度约 V = 16.21 m/s，对应 h = 49V^2/(18g) ≈ 72.902 m。

raw_record.original_question:
A frictionless track contains a loop of radius $R=0.5\,\mathrm{m}$. A small ball of mass $m=2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed at a height $h$ and then released. It collides with another ball of mass $M=5\,\mathrm{kg}$. The coefficient of restitution for the collision is $e=\frac{1}{2}$.

Now consider the alternative case in which the circular loop has a uniform coefficient of friction $\mu=0.6$, while the rest of the path remains frictionless. Assuming the balls are point masses and the collision still has restitution coefficient $e=\frac{1}{2}$, find the minimum value of $h$ such that the ball of mass $M$ is able to move all the way around the loop.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the figure is a smooth downward-sliding track, and a ball of mass m is located at a position with height h from the bottom horizontal track; on the bottom horizontal track there is a ball of mass M; on the right side is a vertical circular loop, with radius R marked, and the bottom of the circular loop is tangent to the horizontal track. Therefore the motion process can be read as: m is released from rest from height h, after sliding down it collides on the horizontal section with the stationary M, and afterward M enters the circular loop and goes around.

Reasoning: The downward-sliding section and the horizontal section before collision have no friction, so the speed of m before collision is u = sqrt(2gh). The collision is a one-dimensional collision, M is initially stationary, and conservation of momentum and coefficient of restitution e=1/2 give the speed of M after collision as V = ((1+e)m/(m+M))u = ((3/2)*2/7)u = 3u/7.

There is uniform friction μ=0.6 inside the circular loop. Let θ=0 be at the bottom of the circular loop, θ=π be at the top, and set y=v^2. When the ball moves on the inside of the circular loop, the normal force is N = M(y/R + g cosθ). The energy differential equation along the arc length R dθ is (1/2)M dy = -MgR sinθ dθ - μN R dθ, therefore y' + 2μy = -2gR(sinθ + μ cosθ).

Use the integrating factor exp(2μθ) to integrate from 0 to π. Let a=2μ, then y(π)e^{aπ} - y(0) = -2gR ∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ, so y(0)=e^{aπ}y(π)+2gR I, where I=∫_0^π e^{aθ}(sinθ + μ cosθ)dθ. The minimum condition is just maintaining contact at the top, that is y(π)=gR.

The integration result is I = ((1-2μ^2)(e^{2μπ}+1))/(4μ^2+1). Substituting μ=0.6: e^{2μπ}=e^{1.2π}≈43.37597, I≈0.28(43.37597+1)/2.44≈5.09282. Therefore V^2=y(0)=gR(e^{1.2π}+2I)≈gR(43.37597+10.18564)=gR(53.56161).

Also V=3u/7, so u=7V/3, h=u^2/(2g)=49V^2/(18g)=49R(53.56161)/18. Substituting R=0.5 m, h≈72.902 m.
